correctness.rationale: Writing h(t)=P(H>t,R>t) and k(t)=P(H>t)f_R(t), direct substitution a²/(4Du) in the two parts of the first-hit integral gives the displayed p, and ∫k=1−p. The kernel has density O(t^(−α−1)), h(t) is regularly varying of index −α with the stated coefficient, and the reset-renewal density u has finite mass q/p. For b=(1+t)^(−α−δ) as in the record, splitting k*b at t/2 proves (k*b)/b→q; since k/b→0 and k vanishes before τ₀, comparison in τ₀-sized time intervals gives u=O(b). The part of u*h past t/2 is o(h) because ∫₀^{t/2}h is bounded, logarithmic, or O(t^(1−α)) according to α, including equality. The early part gives (q/p)h by bounded regular-variation ratios. Replacing u by k^{*n} and inserting 1_{s≥εt} gives respectively q^n h and o(h); hence count tightness and σ(t)/t→0. The absorbing heat kernel in scaled coordinates, divided by erf(a/√(4Dv)), converges pointwise to y exp(−y²/4)/2; since both densities normalize, this also gives convergence in total variation for the one-segment law. The age v=t−σ is asymptotic to t under each fixed count, independent clock censoring leaves the spatial conditional law unchanged, and mixing gives the stated joint limit. Layer-cake integration gives the strict moment boundaries, including logarithmic divergence at equality.
residual_risks: The proof is for fixed positive parameters, not uniform over reset parameters. The supplied numerical checks do not establish conditional joint convergence or a finite-time crossover.

evidence: The probability tail of a light-tailed random sum of independent identically distributed subexponential variables is its expected count times the summand tail.

The wedge result proves geometric completed count and tight unscaled last epoch, with a fair eventual exit-edge mark independent of the limiting past. Its proof contains the same fixed-count early/late convolution split.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Use the geometric total of failed attempts, independently sampled reset-terminated durations, then one independent hit-terminated duration. Their tails are βc/(αq) and c/(2αp) times t^(−α), respectively, by integrating the corresponding marked densities. The random-sum result plus a two-tail convolution gives c/p. The scalar equivalent thus specializes standard theory. The wedge proof is a strong analogue for the count and last epoch, but the threshold is state-triggered; neither its geometry nor its future edge mark gives the Pareto-clock Rayleigh endpoint.

value.rationale: For a standard first-passage benchmark, the evaluated tail and the joint survivor law address different practical questions: mean reset time does not diagnose the tail, and a geometric lifetime count does not tell whether long survivors have undergone many resets. The marked theorem answers the latter at a fixed observation time and predicts the diffusive endpoint independently of the past count. This is useful beyond restating the renewal equation or mean threshold.
residual_risks: No quantitative crossover or claim for the separate ratchet-potential problem; asymptotic shape is not a finite-time estimate.
